decisions.question: How often should another faction's truck pop its smoke dischargers?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 573): raiders' trucks carry no chemfuel to reload, so a truck of theirs comes loaded for one salvo and pops it the first time it is hit while you are a threat.

options.label: Once a visit
options.detail: As built: one salvo each time it comes to a map

options.label: Every hit, 10 s apart
options.detail: Loaded free each time, as often as yours with the switch on

decisions.why: A real truck carries a few reloads at most; smoke every 10 seconds would blind your guns for the whole fight

decisions.question: Without Combat Extended our ring guns feed from steel. Should steel count as rounds in the ammunition locker?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 574): a round is whatever a fitted gun's ammunition allows, as Vehicle Framework itself decides, so a gun truck's steel (and the dischargers' chemfuel) goes in the locker.

options.label: Yes, as built
options.detail: Whatever the truck's guns fire counts as rounds

options.label: No, never raw materials
options.detail: Steel and chemfuel stay ordinary cargo; the locker holds only real ammunition items

decisions.why: It is what those guns actually load; without Combat Extended there are no ammunition items, so 'no' would leave the locker empty

decisions.question: Should the turbocharger fitting be refused on an engine that is already turbocharged as built?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.320.0 (row 576): a built-in turbo is now a part like a fitted one. The fitting is still offered on those engines and adds its x1.2 on top; if the one turbo part fails, both power losses apply (about 0.58 of rated).

options.label: Refuse it there
options.detail: The Fittings window says the engine already has a turbocharger; any already fitted stays until taken off

options.label: Allow it, as now
options.detail: Read as a bigger turbo on top of the built-in one, with the double loss when it fails

decisions.why: One turbo part stands for one turbo; a second fitting on it has no physical meaning and makes the failure harsher than either alone

decisions.question: Should a convoy at a halt (camped or stopped) also be offered the ambush choice, or only one that is driving?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.322.0 (EM44, row 585): only a moving convoy sees the ambush coming and is asked; a halted one gets the game's ambush.

options.label: Only a moving convoy, as built
options.detail: A convoy at a halt is caught standing and fights

options.label: A halted convoy may turn back too
options.detail: No driving through from a standstill, but turning back is offered, at lower odds

options.label: Every convoy is asked
options.detail: Both ways out, at the same odds, whether moving or not

decisions.why: Seeing an ambush coming and getting away at speed both need the convoy to be on the move; a camp is the ambush's best case

decisions.question: Should getting through an ambush cost anything, or is the roll the whole price?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.322.0 (EM44, row 585): a successful drive-through costs nothing; a failed one is the game's ambush.

options.label: Some hits on the way
options.detail: Each vehicle takes light damage to its outer parts, less with armour

options.label: Extra fuel
options.detail: An hour's fuel at full power for the dash

decisions.why: Running a gauntlet in reality costs some hits; armour would then matter twice, which is what the kits are for

decisions.question: Should a survey halt's reading decide the deep ore of a map later opened on that tile (EM32)?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.322.0 (EM31, row 582): a tile's reading is fixed for the tile but is not what a map opened there scatters; the game makes a map's deep ore only when the map is made.

options.label: Yes, as EM32 later
options.detail: A map opened on a read tile shows the read ore as its deep lump, without a scanner

options.label: No
options.detail: The reading stays a guide for the test hole and the bore only

decisions.why: It makes a reading keep its value, which is EM32's whole point; it needs a patch into map generation, so it is its own piece of work
